_comment: CONFORMANCE CORPUS for the credential-NAME matcher, shared by both language suites. The vocabulary in credential-names.json is single-sourced, but the RULE built from it is not: src/credential-names.mjs (npm) and agent_sanitizer/secrets/credential_names.py (PyPI) are hand-written twins, and the language boundary is real - an npm consumer cannot import Python and a wheel cannot import JavaScript, so the executable logic CANNOT be shared. Both modules' own docstrings say the words are the easy part and the rule is where the mistakes are, yet each suite only ever ran its own side: a divergence in segmentation, case folding, run length, scope or the non-secret decline could ship in one ecosystem and not the other, silently. This file is what makes that divergence FAIL instead: test/credential-name-matcher.test.mjs and tests/secrets/test_credential_names.py are each parameterized over these cases and assert their own matcher's answer against the SAME literal expectations. Every `expected` here is hand-written data, never computed from either implementation - a corpus whose expectations come from the code under test agrees with whatever that code does, including its bugs. The noun- and suffix-driven cases are derived from credential-names.json, and both suites assert that every rendered segment and every non-secret segment appears here, so adding a noun to the vocabulary without extending this corpus is a test failure rather than a silent coverage hole. Case fields: `id` (unique), `name` (the variable NAME handed to the matcher), `scope` ("trailing" - the redactor's rule, the noun must be the name's last underscore-delimited run; "any-segment" - the env-scrub's rule, the noun may be any whole run), `declineNonSecret` (apply nonSecretSuffixes to the trailing run: a name ending in one holds an identifier or a public key, not a secret), `expected` (the verdict the predicate must return) and `why` (the reason the verdict is right, so a failing case is diagnosed against intent rather than re-baselined against whichever side broke).
